correctness.rationale: The shared-Hessian component gradient step diagonalizes to an affine contraction \(e^+=q e+t c_i\); each complete epoch is \(e_{k+1}=q^n e_k+tZ_k\) with centered epoch noise. Covariances of two different permutation positions are exactly \(-v/(n-1)\), whereas iid covariances vanish. Independent epochs then yield the exact finite \(K\) second-moment expression (1). Algebraic factorization of two geometric sums establishes the sign for all \(-1<q<1\). Choosing centers along individual eigenvectors proves necessity and mixed ordering. Exact exhaustive enumeration on 123 rational settings corroborated equations, including the reversal witness.

originality.rationale: The motivating 2026 RR guarantee concerns weighted all-inner averages and comparative RATE BOUNDS, not expected individual epoch-terminal objectives. Ying (2018) credits the precursor finite-population covariance identity only for nonnegative scalar or positive-semidefinite matrix weights; its hypothesis excludes the negative multiplier \(q=1-\eta\lambda\). De Sa (2020) provides a general noncommuting counterexample in a noiseless setting, and Dewasurendra treats an all-inner output at small steps. The presently assessed combination of exact signed spectral last-iterate formula and data-uniform iff threshold was not found in inspected sources. The extensive known covariance precursor and possible unindexed equivalent signed-weight calculations are material residual risks.
residual_risks: Ying (2018) already supplies the core covariance polynomial for nonnegative weights; extension to negative weights is algebraically immediate, although the resulting sharp signed phase classification and output comparison are not stated there.
Unindexed or inaccessible publications could derive the same terminal overshoot comparison through signed covariance or linear-recursion analysis.
Only a relevant PDF passage, not the full Shaw–Whalley manuscript, was inspected; it appears bounded to steps below the reciprocal-curvature transition.

value.rationale: Determines a sharp, natural robustness/ordering boundary for two standard sampling strategies on the fundamental shared-curvature noisy quadratic model, directly illuminating the difference between the 2026 averaged-output dominance result and a terminal-checkpoint claim. The all-horizon iff classification and a two-sample sign-reversal witness establish that neither sampling method universally wins in the mixed spectral regime. The value is not the elementary covariance formula itself but the exact decision boundary and its dimension-independent sharpness for the terminal observable. No end-to-end convergence-rate gain or generalization to nonlinear losses is claimed.
